questions.question: What must be checked to show that a subspace U is invariant under a linear operator A?
options: Every vector in V is sent into U by A.
Every vector in U is fixed pointwise by A.
Every vector u in U is sent back into U by A.
Every vector outside U is sent to zero.
questions.explanation: $U$ is invariant under $A$ if every vector $u\in U$ is sent back into $U$ by $A$ (i.e. $Au\in U$).
questions.source_support: Definition: U is invariant under A if $Au∈U$ for every $u∈U$.

It must be a subspace by definition; being closed under $A$ is an additional condition on top of being a subspace.

$A$ stays linear on $U$; the restriction of a linear map to a subspace is still linear.
